quizzes.stem: A team moves a working direct-API request to Google Cloud and keeps the body unchanged. It is refused. Which changes does the page require?

options.a: Add an `anthropic-version` header and remove nothing else from the body
options.b: Keep the model in the payload and send the version as a request header
options.c: Move both the model and the version into the query string of the address
options.d: Name the model in the address and carry the version in the payload

explanation.d: The page says "`model` is not passed in the request body" and that it "is specified in the Google Cloud endpoint URL", while `anthropic_version` goes "in the request body".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "`model` is not passed in the request body", and the version is "rather than as a header".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the model "is specified in the Google Cloud endpoint URL", which is the address path, not a query string.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the version is passed "rather than as a header".

quizzes.stem: A developer calls Claude Opus 5.5 through Bedrock with the identifier `claude-opus-5-5` and gets an error. What fixes it?

options.a: Add the provider prefix so the name starts with anthropic
options.b: Use the dated name that the direct API shows, with no prefix at all
options.c: Use the Vertex form of the name, with an at sign and a date after it
options.d: Send the name in a request header called x-model instead of the body

explanation.a: The page says "Model IDs in Claude in Amazon Bedrock carry an `anthropic.` provider prefix".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the Bedrock ids "carry an `anthropic.` provider prefix" and are not the direct API names.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the at-sign form belongs to Google Cloud, where "`model` is not passed in the request body".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the model stays in the body on Bedrock, "the same request body shape as Anthropic's first-party API".

quizzes.stem: A security team wants no long-lived keys on developer laptops when calling Claude through Bedrock. Which path does the page favour?

options.a: A single shared access key stored with the source code of the project
options.b: Bearer tokens kept in each laptop's configuration file for daily use
options.c: A provisioned service role that the platform assumes for the caller
options.d: An assumed role with a session that lasts for a full working week

explanation.c: The page marks the service role as the recommended path: "Use a Bedrock service role with AWS-managed keys for the most secure, long-lived access".
explanation.b: Ruled out because bearer tokens are "(12-hour maximum, least preferred)".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the service role is the path "for the most secure, long-lived access", with "AWS-managed keys" and no shared key in the source.
explanation.d: Ruled out because an assumed role has "a 12-hour maximum session", not a week.

quizzes.stem: A team on Amazon Bedrock plans nightly bulk jobs through the Message Batches API at half price. What do the docs say?

options.a: The endpoint works there, at the same half price as the direct API itself
options.b: That endpoint is not offered there, so the discount route is unavailable
options.c: The endpoint works there, but at a ten percent premium for the region
options.d: The endpoint works there once the Files API has been enabled first

explanation.b: The Bedrock page lists "API endpoints (Message Batches, Models, Admin, Compliance, Usage and Cost)" under features not supported.
explanation.a: Ruled out because that same list names "API endpoints (Message Batches, Models, Admin, Compliance, Usage and Cost)" as missing.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the premium belongs to regional routing: "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints."
explanation.d: Ruled out because the Files API is itself on the list: "URL sources for images and documents, Files API".

quizzes.stem: A company needs single-region data residency for Claude on Google Cloud and also wants provisioned throughput. Which type of address fits?

options.a: Any kind, since the premium buys residency on all three of them
options.b: The global kind, since it routes to wherever capacity is free today
options.c: The multi-region kind, since it supports provisioned throughput as well
options.d: The regional kind, which is required for both aims and costs 10% more

explanation.d: The page says regional endpoints are "Required for single-region data residency, strict compliance mandates, or provisioned throughput", at the premium.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the global kind "only supports pay-as-you-go traffic (provisioned throughput requires regional endpoints)".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the multi-region kind also "supports pay-as-you-go traffic only".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Global endpoints: Dynamic routing for maximum availability", with "No pricing premium" and no residency choice.

quizzes.stem: A team must pick between the two cloud platforms and needs structured outputs and web search from it. What do the pages show?

options.a: AWS offers web search but not structured outputs, while Google's service lacks web search
options.b: AWS lacks both, while Google's service offers both
options.c: Both platforms offer both features without any exception at all
options.d: Google's service offers structured outputs but lacks web search

explanation.b: The Bedrock list has "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)" and structured outputs among the gaps, and the Google Cloud page lists "Structured outputs" and the "Web search tool" among its supported feature highlights.
explanation.a: Ruled out because Bedrock's list has "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)" as missing.
explanation.c: is ruled out for the same reason: Bedrock lacks "Server-side tools (code execution, web search, web fetch, advisor)".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the Google Cloud page lists them "among its supported feature highlights".

quizzes.stem: A team sends the same traffic through a global endpoint and then a regional endpoint on Bedrock. How do the prices compare?

options.a: The two routes cost the same, since the models behind them are identical
options.b: The specific-region route costs ten percent more than the dynamic one
options.c: The dynamic route costs ten percent more, since it covers more locations
options.d: The specific-region route costs half as much, since it uses idle capacity

explanation.b: The page says "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the same sentence prices the two kinds differently: "Regional endpoints carry a 10% pricing premium over global endpoints."
explanation.c: Ruled out because a global endpoint gives "dynamic routing across all available regions for maximum availability" with no premium.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the regional kind is the one with the premium, "10% pricing premium over global endpoints".

quizzes.stem: build_request is called for Vertex with claude-opus-5-5 and a single named region. What happens?

options.a: It raises PlatformError for the endpoint field, as newer models use other routes
options.b: It builds the URL with the region host, as every model is served by those hosts
options.c: It falls back to the worldwide host without complaint and returns the request
options.d: It raises PlatformError for the model field, as that model id is not known

explanation.a: The page's comment is "Specific regional endpoints support Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier; newer models use the global or multi-region endpoints", and the practice says a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Specific regional endpoints support Claude Sonnet 4.6 and earlier".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the practice states "An unsupported model and endpoint pair is a `PlatformError`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a specific region serves `claude-sonnet-4-6` only", so the model is known and the endpoint is the fault.

quizzes.stem: A team wants the faster output option for its streamed chat, running on Opus 5.5 through AWS. What do the docs say?

options.a: The speed mode is limited to Anthropic's own endpoint
options.b: It works the same on AWS, at the same twice-standard rate
options.c: It works on AWS for the Haiku tier alone, at the standard rate
options.d: It works on AWS once the beta header has been sent in the call

explanation.a: The page says fast mode "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".
explanation.b: Ruled out because fast mode "is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the same sentence has no exception by tier: "is available on the Claude API (first-party) only".
explanation.d: Ruled out because a header does not change that: "it is not available on Claude Platform on AWS or partner-operated cloud platforms".

quizzes.stem: A team's Bedrock traffic needs 4 million input tokens per minute. What do the docs say?

options.a: It sits beyond every limit, so a second account is needed
options.b: It fits inside the default, so nothing extra is asked of anyone
options.c: It exceeds the default but stays beneath the requestable ceiling
options.d: It follows the direct API quota rather than the cloud one

explanation.c: The page gives "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and "You can request up to 5 million input TPM and 500,000 output TPM without additional Anthropic approval."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Default quota is 2 million input tokens per minute (TPM)." and 4 million exceeds it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "You can request up to 5 million input TPM" covers 4 million.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "AWS enforces requests-per-minute (RPM) limits on the Bedrock side".
